claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO introduces strong phonon-scattering centers that disrupt coherent lattice vibrations.
SRO can locally stiffen the lattice.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy capable of exhibiting SRO.
AlxCrCoFeNi with x < 0.5 is an example of a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Controlled annealing or compositional tuning can enhance SRO without causing long-range phase separation.
Phonon transport dominates thermal conductivity from 300 K to 1000 K in the proposed alloys.
AlxCrCoFeNi is predicted to be single-phase A1 for 0 < x < 0.5.
AlxCrCoFeNi exhibits substantial chemical clustering over a wide temperature range when x < 0.5.
The relevant SRO motifs can consist of Al-rich clusters or specific atomic-pair correlations.
SRO creates mass-fluctuation and force-constant disorder distinct from that of the random-alloy baseline.
Ordered regions resonantly scatter mid-to-high-frequency phonons because their local vibrational modes and mass distributions differ from those of the surrounding matrix.
SRO increases the phonon-scattering rate and decreases the phonon mean free path.
An SRO-enhanced sample will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than a compositionally and microstructurally matched disordered sample.
The SRO-induced conductivity suppression will be strongest at intermediate temperatures before phonon-phonon scattering becomes dominant.
Long-range intermetallic precipitation would introduce phase-boundary or grain-boundary transport effects distinct from SRO scattering.
Mo-Nb-Ta-W alloys possess significant atomic-mass variance and already have strong mass disorder.
SRO affects dislocation mobility in BCC MoNbTaW, enhancing edge-dislocation mobility while reducing screw-dislocation double-kink nucleation.
The cited evidence does not directly quantify the effect of SRO on phonon scattering or thermal conductivity in RHEAs.
If greater measured SRO produces equal or higher lattice thermal conductivity under matched density and grain size, the proposed scattering-dominated mechanism is falsified.

contradictions.description: AlxCrCoFeNi with x < 0.5 is presented as a BCC example in the initial state, but the conditions identify the same low-Al range as single-phase A1; the cited record explicitly equates A1 with FCC and predicts A1 for x < 0.5.

The proposed experiment treats MoNbTaW and Al0.1CrCoFeNi as interchangeable refractory-alloy examples, although the cited phase evidence places Al0.1CrCoFeNi in the FCC A1 regime rather than the stated BCC refractory initial-state regime.
